html:
SMTO-LEG-0003 — SMTO's license agreement files don't match this version

GUID: 212a9c49-dad4-4985-930a-394cc2c906c7
Slug: eula-definition-conflict
Domain: LEG · Subsystem: leg

What happened

  • SMTO found that the license agreement included with this installation was changed or doesn't match the copy it saved earlier, so it stopped instead of showing the wrong terms. Your past acceptance records were not changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Run the SMTO installer again, or install the latest official release, so the agreement files return to their original form. This check fails when the agreement files that come with SMTO were edited or are out of date.
  2. If SMTO was installed from a development or test build, or someone edited its files, ask the person who installed it to switch to an official release. Each agreement version must always have the same text, so an edited or test copy conflicts with the copy SMTO saved before.
  3. If it still stops, open Technical details in this panel and select Copy error details. The error alone does not establish a repair you can safely perform yourself, so whoever publishes SMTO needs these details.

What success looks like

  • The startup screen reaches Ready, and the agreement opens from Settings › Licenses and legal.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied details to the person who installed SMTO; the fix has to come from the SMTO publisher. Don't edit the agreement files, and don't delete SMTO's settings data; it holds your acceptance history.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Agreement construction failed: the packaged EULA file's SHA-256 differs from DOCUMENT_SHA256, its presentation template drifted, or the stored legal_eula_documents row for this version holds a different hash.

What this means

  • Agreement construction detects a modified unreviewed template/hash, or a stored agreement version is already bound to different canonical content. These are product document-identity and admission checks. Diagnostics neither accept terms for a user nor change agreement/acceptance records; publisher defects require publisher repair.

Why this can happen

  • Agreement construction detects a modified unreviewed template/hash, or a stored agreement version is already bound to different canonical content.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare shipped template, canonical digest and stored version binding without editing acceptance history.

How to fix it

  • Compare the eula-*.md file named by SMTO_EULA_VERSION and eula-presentation.md in src/agent_runtime/legal/ with the released package (the RuntimeError comes from current_agreement, Agreement._display_template or EulaService.init). Reinstall the unmodified release, or have the publisher ship a new version string with matching content and hash; keep legal_eula_documents and legal_eula_acceptance rows intact.
  • The publisher must review the agreement definition and publish the intended version and matching content. Keep existing acceptance records intact.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The publisher supplies a reviewed consistent version/content pair and existing acceptance records remain intact.

What not to do

  • Do not delete evidence or invent a configuration change for an unexplained internal failure.

Technical notes

  • These are product document-identity and admission checks. Diagnostics neither accept terms for a user nor change agreement/acceptance records; publisher defects require publisher repair.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
